intro: This page is the board and toolchain matrix. It is taken from `config/core-recipes.toml`, `config/core-library.toml`, `profiles/native-integration-dev.toml`, the per-core `toolchain.lock` files, the misteross producers, and the docs those files point at. A cell that is not in those sources is marked unverified or TBD.

The bootstrap image installs `fes.menu` and the pinned splash bitstream. Every playable core is a catalog install. Library standing `supported` is not a claim that the current bitstream has kit acceptance. Dated notes under `docs/validation/` accept only the artifact they name.

Tiers are derived from the tier role, owned RTL dates and media generation; kit notes are recorded but do not set a tier. Catalog standing is stored on each row as a weak signal and is not an input. The owned-RTL activity snapshot is as of 2026-10-29; role, media and dated kit notes may be updated later. The recent cutoff is 2026-10-16. The window starts 2026-08-30. A tier_override with reason Deano 2026-10-29 replaces the derived tier.

`quality_tier` on each row records the quality ladder that [the forward plan](plans/forward-plan.md) already decided for DE10-Nano cells. It is not the freshness `tier`, and it is not release scope. `check_level` says how much per-change evidence each row is expected to carry, under the hard rule beside D12 in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) that Deano accepted on 2026-11-15. It never lowers a gate on work being done to a core.

tiers.label: Firmware
tiers.meaning: Boot package or pinned idle RBF.

tiers.label: Current
tiers.meaning: Owned RTL on or after 2026-10-16, and media is not the old generation.

tiers.label: Aging
tiers.meaning: Owned RTL in the 60-day window, before 2026-10-16.

tiers.label: Stale
tiers.meaning: No owned RTL in the 60-day window.

tiers.label: Bring-up
tiers.meaning: The machine is still in bring-up. Its package is a diagnostic or development profile, and what it is accepted for is the dated evidence on the row.

tiers.label: Bring-up (queued)
tiers.meaning: No package yet. Queued by Deano 2026-10-29.

tiers.label: Shared
tiers.meaning: CPU RTL used by other cores. Not a system package.

tiers.label: Demo
tiers.meaning: Registered demo package, not a machine.

policy: Labels follow the accepted Quartus policy in [Quartus-built cores](design/quartus-cores.md) (issue #1163). `oss` is the Debian-style main set: Yosys + nextpnr-mistral. `quartus` is the non-free set: a proprietary toolchain. A core build is supposed to say which one made it, so an all-OSS selection can exclude every Quartus build. `FES_OSS_ONLY` is not implemented. Current registered recipes and package selection build the OSS lane only. A failed OSS route never falls back to Quartus.

Both labelled builds ship only when the published rule is met, on the same RTL and the same target clocks. Either every Quartus sign-off seed closes a required clock that an OSS sign-off seed misses, or the best complete-seed Fmax is at least 15% higher on any required clock: `100 × (Quartus best − OSS best) / OSS best`. Otherwise the core ships OSS only. No registered recipe declares a `toolchains` list yet, so no core ships both builds today. The i386 far-transfer numbers (about 40%) remain the worked example of a gap large enough for that rule. i386, pc386 and PC/XT are separately Quartus-primary; their nextpnr builds are advisory.

DE25-Nano (Agilex 5) is Quartus-only (policy); shell pending. policy: Deano 2026-10-29. Rows with a DE10 board bitstream show Quartus; rows without a board bitstream show no DE25 toolchain cell. Agilex 5 has no OSS reverse-engineering, so there is no OSS toolchain for that device. nextpnr-mistral targets Cyclone V (`5CSEBA6U23I7` in [the DE10-Nano board note](../sources/misteross/boards/de10nano/README.md)). Quartus Pro 24.1 or later is the first release that supports Agilex 5 ([Quartus-built cores](design/quartus-cores.md)). `sources/misteross/boards/de25nano` may be absent or present; the checker treats that landing as expected. Per-core DE25 cells stay on the policy line until the shell is on this branch and those cells are re-verified.

i386, pc386 and PC/XT use Quartus (primary, policy). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. nextpnr builds are advisory, and a nextpnr miss there is filed as a nextpnr issue, not a blocker. PC/XT has a registered Quartus diagnostic package producer and an advisory nextpnr diagnostic. pc386 retains pack-only nextpnr synthesis, and i386 retains the Quartus 17.0.2 fit of its Yosys netlist ([i386 CPU design](../sources/misteross/docs/i386-cpu-design.md), DeanoC/nextpnr#300). Those tree facts do not change the primary label.

ColecoVision still uses the old media handling. Its example arcade room has an empty-library status when no matching titles are available. Updating that handling is low priority and is folded into the wider Coleco work (for example Adam support). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. The checked-in factory recipe is the format-4 ROM map, and it strips the blob and blob-stream mailboxes that the older Coleco producers still declare.

cores.quartus: Quartus (primary, policy). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. nextpnr builds are advisory, and a nextpnr miss is filed as a nextpnr issue, not a blocker. `scripts/build_fes_pc386_quartus.py` seals the development package `fes.pc386`, the machine with `fes_i386_cpu`, with Quartus 17.0.2 from the pc386 lock's Yosys netlist.
cores.features: Media: the runtime writes an ATA disk image into the DDR window through the fes.computer 1.1 mailbox and `fes_computer_storage` while execution is held, with a commit CRC pass (`pc386_disk`); the floppy controller (`pc386_fdc`) serves drives A: and B: on IRQ 6 and DMA channel 2. Input: fes.keyboard.hid through the HID row model (`pc386_hid_keyboard` inside the 8042) to the PS/2 keyboard (set 2 with XLAT, typematic), and fes.mouse.relative to the PS/2 aux mouse. HDMI: 720p presenter and display plane. Audio: PC speaker, OPL2 and Sound Blaster. CPU: `fes_i386_cpu` with a speed governor that takes its preset, frequency and turbo from the `fes.pc386.machine` record. x87: since slice 2 (#1768) the 387's state, its interface to the CPU, the AT board's error path and the loads, stores and conversions are built inside `fes_i386_cpu`; its arithmetic is slices 3 to 5 and is not built. Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Phases M1-M5 are done. M5's development package `fes.pc386` (`make build-fes-pc386-quartus`, not a registered recipe and not a catalog package) puts `fes_i386_cpu` in the machine. On seal 254b2bf5 of merge 317310c81 (6 November, Kit B, `max`): a DOOM level played to its exit switch and on into E1M2, a Wolfenstein 3D level played through to floor 2, and Ultima VII Black Gate and Serpent Isle saves loaded after a relaunch. On seal 650bc477 of main 65ec1f22a (10 November, Kit B): FreeDOS with the kit's date and time, Wolfenstein 3D above 30 fps, Ultima VI's speaker pitch at 286-12 and the Black Gate save and load at 386DX-25 pass again; the Wolfenstein 3D playthrough was not rerun, and Serpent Isle's save and load passed in seven launches of eight, the eighth black throughout (#1494). That pitch pass is a regression comparison against the earlier kit run, not a reference: against the named 86Box 286-12 reference the effects play about 2.4 semitones flat, which fails (#1837). Windows for Workgroups 3.11 reaches Program Manager in 386 enhanced mode on build 6ef05309, and Linux 0.99.15, 1.2.13 and 2.0.0 reach a login and a root shell on build 9d784de2, each its own 12 November seal of main; Windows 3.11 is a standing check on each change's seal. Also owed on #1368: Ultima VI's walking speed at 286-12, which is not measurable by any method tried so far and is qualified by how well that preset is calibrated (#1840), and Ultima VII's NPC pace, which is not established and is carried forward as #1853. Serpent Isle's black capture is #1494. The forward plan puts pc386 at tier 1 when #1368 and #1494 close.

cores.label: `fes_i386_cpu`
cores.router: nextpnr routes of this CPU are parked (#1235), and the Phase 1 spike numbers in the CPU design doc are labelled historical. Not a package producer and not a recipe row.
cores.quartus: Quartus (primary, policy). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. nextpnr builds are advisory, and a nextpnr miss is filed as a nextpnr issue, not a blocker; since #1235 no new nextpnr route of this CPU is made at all. Quartus 17.0.2 fits the same Yosys netlist (`scripts/quartus_fes_i386.py`), and every current seal of the CPU comes through the pc386 package. The far-transfer record, about 69-74 MHz nextpnr against about 98-104 MHz Quartus, is the historical spike behind that policy (DeanoC/nextpnr#300, `docs/i386-cpu-design.md`). Recipe and package selection for a labelled variant are not implemented.
cores.features: Not a system package. No media, HDMI, Bluetooth or mesh of its own. The twelve-stage F1-WB pipeline, the L1s and BIU, protected mode and Phase 4's speed work (BTB, return stack, indirect prediction, early ALU and load forwarding) are built; Phase 5 (paging, V86, task switches and the debug registers) is in progress under tracker #1548. The 387 is further on than a plan: since x87 slice 2 (#1768) its state, CPU interface, AT error path, loads, stores and conversions are built in `fes_i386_cpu`, with the arithmetic in slices 3 to 5. The pc386 machine is its consumer: the development package `fes.pc386` seals it with Quartus 17.0.2, and that seal is where this RTL's kit evidence is recorded.
cores.notes: Shared CPU RTL. Device `5CSEBA6U23I7` in the spike harness. Yosys pin `e240a465` is newer than the repository lock's `3a5accbd`; it is the pc386 lock's pin, so one Yosys reads the CPU (#1581 D2, S4).

unverified.where: Every row with a pad or keyboard
unverified.detail: Bluetooth HID/HoG pairing is a host evdev path in the FogCast README. No per-core Bluetooth interface was found.
Launch, library and mesh are host services. No per-core mesh capability flag was found, so this page does not claim that any core is in or out of the mesh.

No recipe records a completed OSS-versus-Quartus sign-off comparison against the 15% rule. i386 is the worked example of the gap and is Quartus-primary by policy; it is not a registered core. Which other current cores would qualify to ship a Quartus variant is unverified.

Core status and the validation notes bind acceptance to named packages. This matrix does not copy those package ids forward. Which rows Deano wants marked HIL-verified for the bytes in the tree is open.

tier_rules: As of 2026-10-29. Window 2026-08-30 through that day. Recent cutoff 2026-10-16.

Owned RTL: a commit that changes that core's rtl/ and whose subject names the core, or where that core holds at least half of the commit's RTL paths and at least two files. A one-file edit inside another core's commit is not owned RTL.
Catalog standing is recorded and is not read by the tier rule.
firmware, shared, demo, reference and bring-up come from tier_role, not from dates.
Otherwise a play row is current when owned RTL is on or after the cutoff, aging when owned RTL is in the window before the cutoff, and stale when it has none.
last_hil_pass is a designated-kit note. It does not by itself set the tier. A host seal or a simulation PASS is not a kit pass.
A play row with media_gen old and owned RTL on or after the recent cutoff derives to unresolved. That result is not a displayed tier. A tier_override with reason Deano 2026-10-29 replaces it.
Coleco derives to unresolved and is Aging by that override. Work toward Current is in progress and still needs work (media handling and the wider Coleco work).
Spectrum and Atari ST derive to current. The same override confirms that tier. Their kit HIL pass on the latest RTL is pending and expected soon.
C64 NTSC and Atari STE have no package. Their override tier is bring-up-queued.
Spectrum +2 is a ROM variant of fes.spectrum128 (kind rom). It is the same core and the same model, with a different ROM. Deano 2026-10-29.

quality_tier and check_level are not inputs to the tier rule. quality_tier cites the forward plan's ladder; check_level is derived from it, from tier_role and from the bring-up-queued tier, which is the one place a tier feeds the check level. check_level carries the hard rule beside D12 in AGENTS.md, accepted by Deano 2026-11-15.
needs_deano: SMS and SG-1000 are outside the first-party catalog; their development recipes remain registered. Tier aging uses owned RTL on 2026-10-06 and kit diagnostics on 2026-09-29. The catalog flag was not used.
Pong catalog standing is supported. No owned RTL in the 60-day window, so the tier is stale. The catalog flag was not used.
ZX80, TS1000 and TS1500 share the ZX81 shell. Kit notes name fes.zx81 (2026-10-22), not those three. The 2026-10-25 model commit is after that note.
Apple II kit diagnostic is 2026-09-27. Owned RTL is 2026-10-06 (#549). No later kit note was found.
Open issues on each row are title matches, not a full blocker audit.

ColecoVision is check_level reduced by the ladder (2-pending) while being under active work. Reduced exempts only sweeps it is not about, but if Coleco should carry full evidence for every sweep as well, the ladder has to place it rather than name its condition.
RAM Tester is outside the ladder as a utility and is under active timing work (#1832, #1767). The same question as Coleco: reduced for sweeps, or full because the memory path is shared.

SG-1000's newest owned RTL is an ABI migration (#1755) and Apple II's is the original-glyph campaign (#1819). The owned-RTL rule counts both as core activity, so the freshness tier cannot be read as development activity on either row.

Does a mechanical RTL sweep count as touching a core? #1714 edited eight RTL files across five cores to remove one obsolete mailbox. Under the wording here it touches each core's own RTL, so every gate applies and reduced buys nothing on it. If sweeps like that should also be exempt, the wording has to say so, and D12 does not cover them because they change RTL.

Should the 2-pending rows (Coleco, SMS, SG-1000, Apple II) carry full evidence on a closure sweep anyway? They are reduced here because the forward plan names no tier for them until they meet the port.

Should the per-family representative scoping be a rule as well? On PR #1862 the sibling variants (zx80, ts1000, ts1500, spectrum128, spectrum-plus3, pentagon) were dropped from the route conditions along with the held-back cores; check_level keeps them at full because they are tier 1.

fes.riscv's snapshot last_rtl_change (2026-10-05) reads its core directory only. `dcfa92c98` (2026-10-21) changed `fes_rv32_cpu.sv` in the shared riscv directory that this row holds under `paths`, and the subject names riscv, so whether that commit should move the row to Current inside the same snapshot is open. The owned-RTL check runs on shared rows only, so nothing catches it either way.

A pending quality_tier has to be re-read by hand when its condition closes. The checker reads the forward plan's Tiers section and fails if a cited sentence moves, goes or is restated, and if the plan stops naming #1368, #1494 or the port condition; it cannot see a superseding decision written in new words. So when #1368 and #1494 close, pc386's 1-pending becomes tier 1 and its check level does not change, but the row still needs editing.

fes.pc386 keeps tier_role bring-up, so its tier stays Bring-up although its package runs games, Windows and Linux on a kit. The alternative is tier_role play, which would derive Current from its RTL dates; it is not a registered recipe or a catalog package, so this page kept bring-up and reworded that tier's meaning instead.

note: In force. Deano accepted it on 2026-11-15, and the rule itself is the hard rule beside D12 in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md): a core at `check_level: reduced` owes a closure sweep only D12's netlist comparison, which is still measured and recorded, and not the RBF reproduction, the timing and seal gate or the HIL. This page is where the levels are listed; AGENTS.md is where the obligation is written. Neither lowers a gate on work being done to a core.

`quality_tier` cites a decision rather than inventing a taxonomy: the ladder, its bars, the tier 1 set, the two pending placements and the utilities outside it are all decided in [the forward plan](plans/forward-plan.md) (tiers apply per (core, board) cell; DE10-Nano is the tier 1 board). Where the plan names a condition rather than a tier, this page records the condition: pc386 is `1-pending` and not tier 2, and Coleco, SMS, SG-1000 and Apple II are `2-pending`, because the plan names no tier for any of them before their condition is met. The freshness `tier` on each row answers a different question and stays derived from dates, so a tier 1 cell can be Aging and a row off the ladder can have RTL from this week.

`check_level` says what a change owes each row, and the D12 conditions are what it is about. `full`: every change that moves the core's `BUILD_ID` carries that core's own evidence, all three D12 conditions included. `reduced`: on a change that does not touch the core's own RTL, programs, lock or placement recipe, the netlist comparison (D12's first condition, which needs no GPU route) is still expected, and the RBF reproduction, the timing and seal gate and the HIL (its second and third, and the reseal the rule falls back to) are not. If that comparison fails, the core counts as touched and keeps every gate, which is what D12 already says. A change aimed at the core, and any change that ships it, keeps every gate. `via-consumer`: the row is RTL, not a package, so its evidence rides with the packages that embed it. `none`: there is no built artifact to carry evidence for yet.

The cost this answers is a closure sweep, which is what D12 covers: a change with no RTL that moves a core's `BUILD_ID` through its build record or source closure. As of 2026-11-15, PR #1862 edits five producer scripts and one shared helper, touches no RTL, QSF, SDC, lock or placement recipe, and moves the `BUILD_ID` of all 14 cores whose producers import a changed file, so D12 applies to each of them. Its first condition was measured for all 14; Deano scoped the route-based second and third on 2026-11-15 to the firmware plus one representative per affected machine family, leaving `fes.pong`, `fes.ramtest`, `fes.coleco` and `fes.riscv` unmeasured because they are not shipped. This rule is close to that call but not the same one: it drops the same two conditions for the same held-back cores by rule, while it keeps at full the sibling variants that call also dropped (zx80, ts1000, ts1500, spectrum128, spectrum-plus3, pentagon). Whether the representative scoping should be a rule too is a separate question.

The levels never lower a gate on work being done to a core: a netlist that is not byte-identical, a change that touches the core's own RTL, programs, lock or placement recipe, and any change that ships it, all put that core back under the full rule. AGENTS.md's hard rule against relaxing a timing or seal check stands above this one and is unchanged.

levels.label: Full
levels.meaning: Every change that moves the core's `BUILD_ID` carries that core's own evidence.

levels.label: Reduced
levels.meaning: On a sweep the core is not about, its netlist comparison still holds; the RBF repeat, seal gate and HIL do not. A moved netlist keeps every gate.

levels.label: Via consumer
levels.meaning: Not a package. Evidence rides with the packages that embed it.
